producer_report.summary: Each study is now validated against its own pin. In rules.rs the firstmate-only constants are replaced by check_study(dir, pin_env, mount) and check_studies(root, ...). The kept test checks conventions for every studies/*/ directory: a 40-hex pin, study_id equal to the directory name, a quote on each file source, claim tags, no guard of none said to be checked by code, and no UNRESOLVED / 'not examined' placeholder outside sources[].quote. Each failure names the offending id. Full validation against pinned-source/ runs only for the study whose pin.json URL and SHA equal ATHENA_PIN_URL / ATHENA_PIN_SHA, and the result is compared with validation.json. A same-URL pin with a different SHA fails, naming the study. With no pair set, only conventions run, and a WARNING line is printed when a tree is mounted but no study matched. Tests on temp copies and on a tree rebuilt from a study's own citations cover the four faults, the matching route, tampered records and quotes, a second study directory, and the warning logic. Study::admit now refuses a change spanning two studies/<id>/ directories (study-one-directory) and any path outside one study directory and CHANGELOG.md (study-outside-directory); build output keeps its own single violation. xtask/tests/policy.rs gains boundary_scan_file: it blanks only a claim's source quote in studies/<id>/claims.json, matched by regex and decoded with serde_json, before word matching. Machine-path fragments are always matched on the raw text. The new tests plant split-string words. producer.md states the three conventions and still fits the recorded producer budget, so docs/system-facts.md is untouched. CHANGELOG.md has the entry. Nothing under studies/ and no athena.toml changed.

open_issues: Host: no code in this repository sets ATHENA_PIN_URL or ATHENA_PIN_SHA for study checks. Until the pinning change does, the kept test checks conventions only and prints a WARNING when pinned-source/ is mounted. The study verifier prompt's line that code already ran the validation rules does not hold until then. The CHANGELOG entry says so.

User question: should rationale-card source quotes and a card's authors_say also be exempt from the boundary scan, and authors_say from the placeholder check? I exempted only claims.json source quotes from the boundary scan and only sources[].quote from the placeholder check, as the request names.

User question: studies sharing one repository URL cannot be told apart by ATHENA_PIN_*, which carries no study id. Another study of that URL with a different SHA therefore fails the kept test, as the request asks. Should it be skipped once the pinning change can pass the study id?
The mounted-tree case (firstmate against the real pinned-source/) was not run here. Only the rebuilt-tree route was run.
Admission now refuses a study job's change to any path outside one studies/<id>/ and CHANGELOG.md. I could not measure the replay refusal share; Athena measures it.
mistakes: My first producer.md draft was 40 tokens over the recorded budget. I trimmed it in two passes using the budgets test.
The first version of the new tests used `[claim.clone()]`, which failed clippy. I fixed it.
learnings: firstmate's claims.json has 79 sources, all of kind file. No quote holds an escaped newline. Neither study placeholder word occurs in any firstmate study file.

The study producer set measured 1058, then 1045, before the final wording reached the recorded 1043 maximum. The budget test therefore forces the prompt edit to be net-small without touching docs/system-facts.md.
The Bash hook here allows only cargo, chmod, git, ls, mv and rm, with no pipes or $? substitution.
The workspace denies unsafe_code, so tests cannot set env vars. The pin pair and the mount are passed to check_study as arguments, and only the kept test reads the environment.
Clippy's cloned_ref_to_slice_refs rejects `[x.clone()]` in assert_eq!; use `[x.as_str()]` instead.
